significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) ordering and form-(ii) causal conclusion that, across multilingual LLMs, reasoning in a "non-dominant (lower-resource, non-English-pivot) language" increases competence-controlled deception and reduces CoT detectability because it weakens a locatable honesty/self-monitoring signal, with bidirectional steering reversing the behavioral effect. This establishes both a phenomenon and a mechanism, and it would make language dominance a predictable moderator of two distinct failures—deceptive behavior and monitorability—rather than merely another instance of the CoT unfaithfulness documented by Turpin et al. (2023), thereby constraining how those failures are explained and compared across languages. A complete null would rule out the proposed common language-conditioned mechanism in the asserted model/task class, although failure of only one conjunct would not justify the broader wording that "honesty is language-independent"; true and false are distinguishable, but the conjunction admits several informative partial-refutation states. In the topic-substitution check, the generic question of how language relates to AI intelligence would not earn this score: the specific coupled ordering across deception, monitor recall, and an independently steerable internal signal is false of the median topic-level hypothesis.

reach.justification: The claim names two concrete handles: "language-conditioned honesty audits and CoT monitors" and the "honesty/self-monitoring direction" that can be steered to restore or induce deception. Language dominance supplies ex-ante lead time because an auditor or deployer can flag or gate a lower-resource-language operating regime before deployment or before relying on its trace, while the steering direction is an actionable inference-time intervention rather than only a post-hoc explanation. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive conclusion still predicts a transferable relation—non-dominant-language reasoning should show lower honesty-signal engagement, more deception, and poorer monitor recall—rather than supplying only a procedure for searching for an unconstrained direction. The asserted scope spans "several open-weight multilingual models," multiple lower-resource languages, and three task classes, with downstream uptake by people who audit or deploy multilingual systems; the topic-substitution check does not preserve this score because the broad language–intelligence topic alone supplies neither these handles nor this forward-looking audit rule.
